title: Present Simple Tense
simpleExplanation: Present simple describes habits, facts, and general truths. Add -s for he/she/it.
detailedExplanation: Present simple is used for habitual actions, permanent situations, and general truths. Most verbs add -s for third person singular (he/she/it): work→works. Verbs ending in -s, -sh, -ch, -x, -o add -es: go→goes, watch→watches. Have becomes has. Negatives use don't/doesn't + base verb. Questions use do/does.
usage: I work every day. | She works in an office.
avoidWhen: Don't use for actions happening right now (use present continuous).
simpleExplanation_en: Present simple describes habits, facts, and general truths. Add -s for he/she/it.
simpleExplanation_id: Present simple menyatakan kebiasaan, fakta, dan kebenaran umum. Tambah -s untuk he/she/it.

title: Present Continuous Tense
simpleExplanation: Present continuous describes actions happening now or around now. Form: am/is/are + verb-ing.
detailedExplanation: Use present continuous for actions in progress now, temporary situations, and future arrangements. Form: subject + am/is/are + verb-ing. Spelling: drop final -e (make→making), double final consonant after short vowel (sit→sitting), -ie becomes -y (lie→lying). Not used with stative verbs (know, like, want).
usage: I am studying now. | She is eating lunch.
avoidWhen: Don't use with stative verbs like know, like, want, need.
commonMistakes: Using with stative verbs (I am knowing - wrong)
simpleExplanation_en: Present continuous describes actions happening now or around now. Form: am/is/are + verb-ing.
simpleExplanation_id: Present continuous menyatakan aksi sedang terjadi sekarang atau sekitar sekarang. Bentuk: am/is/are + kata kerja-ing.
detailedExplanation_en: Use present continuous for actions in progress now, temporary situations, and future arrangements. Form: subject + am/is/are + verb-ing. Spelling: drop final -e (make→making), double final consonant after short vowel (sit→sitting), -ie becomes -y (lie→lying). Not used with stative verbs (know, like, want).
detailedExplanation_id: Pakai untuk aksi berlangsung sekarang, situasi sementara, dan rencana masa depan. Bentuk: subjek + am/is/are + kata kerja-ing. Ejaan: buang -e akhir (make jadi making), gandakan konsonan akhir.
usage_en: I am studying now. | She is eating lunch.
usage_id: I am studying now. | She is eating lunch.
avoidWhen_en: Don't use with stative verbs like know, like, want, need.

commonMistakes_en: Using with stative verbs (I am knowing - wrong)
commonMistakes_id: Dipakai dengan kata kerja statif (I am knowing - salah)

title: Past Simple Tense
simpleExplanation: Past simple describes completed actions in the past. Regular verbs add -ed, irregular verbs have special forms.
detailedExplanation: Use past simple for finished actions at a specific past time. Regular verbs: add -ed (work→worked). Spelling: double consonant (stop→stopped), -y→-ied (study→studied). Irregular verbs must be memorized (go→went, eat→ate, see→saw). Negatives: didn't + base verb. Questions: Did + subject + base verb?
usage: I worked yesterday. | She went to school.
avoidWhen: Don't use for actions with present relevance (use present perfect).

simpleExplanation_id: Past simple menyatakan aksi selesai di masa lampau. Kata kerja reguler tambah -ed, tak beraturan punya bentuk khusus.
detailedExplanation_en: Use past simple for finished actions at a specific past time. Regular verbs: add -ed (work→worked). Spelling: double consonant (stop→stopped), -y→-ied (study→studied). Irregular verbs must be memorized (go→went, eat→ate, see→saw). Negatives: didn't + base verb. Questions: Did + subject + base verb?
detailedExplanation_id: Pakai untuk aksi selesai pada waktu lampau tertentu. Reguler: tambah -ed (work jadi worked). Ejaan: gandakan konsonan (stop jadi stopped), -y jadi -ied (study jadi studied). Kata kerja tak beraturan harus dihafal.

avoidWhen_id: Jangan untuk aksi yang relevan sekarang (pakai present perfect).
commonMistakes_id: Memakai -ed dengan kata kerja tak beraturan

title: Articles (a, an, the)
simpleExplanation: Use 'a/an' for non-specific singular nouns, 'the' for specific nouns. 'An' before vowel sounds.
detailedExplanation: 'A/an' introduce new, non-specific singular countable nouns. Use 'an' before vowel sounds (an apple, an hour). 'The' refers to specific nouns known to speaker and listener, unique things, or mentioned before. No article with plural/uncountable for general meaning, or with proper nouns (names, countries, cities - with exceptions).
usage: I have a dog. The dog is black. | An apple a day.
avoidWhen: Don't use 'the' for general plural/uncountable (I like dogs, not 'the dogs').

examples.text: I saw a cat. The cat was sleeping.
examples.translation: I saw a cat. The cat was sleeping.
examples.translation_en: I saw a cat. The cat was sleeping.

title: Prepositions of Time (at, in, on)
simpleExplanation: Use 'at' for clock times, 'in' for months/years/seasons, 'on' for days and dates.
detailedExplanation: 'At' for specific times (at 5 o'clock, at noon, at night). 'In' for longer periods (in January, in 2020, in summer, in the morning/afternoon/evening). 'On' for days and dates (on Monday, on June 5th, on my birthday). Exceptions: at night, at the weekend (UK)/on the weekend (US).
avoidWhen: Don't mix them up (not 'in Friday' or 'at Monday').
commonMistakes: Confusing at night vs in the morning

title: Question Formation
simpleExplanation: Form questions with auxiliary verbs (do/does/did/is/are) or question words (what, where, when, who, why, how).
detailedExplanation: Yes/no questions: Auxiliary + subject + verb (Do you like...? Is she...?). Wh-questions: Question word + auxiliary + subject + verb (Where do you live?). Present simple uses do/does, past simple uses did. With 'be', invert subject and verb (Are you...? Was he...?). Who/What as subject don't need auxiliary (Who lives here?).
usage: Do you speak English? | Where are you from?
avoidWhen: Don't use auxiliary with 'be' as main verb.
simpleExplanation_en: Form questions with auxiliary verbs (do/does/did/is/are) or question words (what, where, when, who, why, how).
simpleExplanation_id: Bentuk pertanyaan dengan kata kerja bantu (do/does/did/is/are) atau kata tanya (what, where, when, who, why, how).
detailedExplanation_en: Yes/no questions: Auxiliary + subject + verb (Do you like...? Is she...?). Wh-questions: Question word + auxiliary + subject + verb (Where do you live?). Present simple uses do/does, past simple uses did. With 'be', invert subject and verb (Are you...? Was he...?). Who/What as subject don't need auxiliary (Who lives here?).
detailedExplanation_id: Pertanyaan ya/tidak: kata bantu + subjek + kata kerja (Do you like...? Is she...?). Pertanyaan Wh-: kata tanya + kata bantu + subjek + kata kerja (Where do you live?). Present simple pakai do/does, past simple pakai did.
usage_en: Do you speak English? | Where are you from?
usage_id: Do you speak English? | Where are you from?
avoidWhen_en: Don't use auxiliary with 'be' as main verb.
avoidWhen_id: Jangan pakai kata bantu dengan be sebagai kata kerja utama.
